newsitem.title: USA: Ajay year loss due to Palm Springs.
newsitem.headline: Ajay year loss due to Palm Springs.

text.p: Ajay Sports Inc, posting a wider loss for full-year 1996 than in 1995, said Friday more than 65 percent of the loss was due to its Palm Springs Golf operation.
For the year, Ajay reported a loss of $0.09 per share compared to a year-ago loss of $0.03. Sales rose to $24.3 million from $18.7 million.

The company also said it continues to work with new lenders to replace its current credit facility. On April 14, 1997, the company's lender agreed to waive a previously announced bank loan technical default and restore Ajay's credit limit to $13.5 million from $12 million.

"The losses at Palm Springs Golf and the restricted bank financing, which was a direct result of the losses at Palm Springs, have had a significant impact on Ajay's profitability and flexibility for the past 15 months," said chairman Thomas Itin in a statement.

"At Palm Springs Golf, a number of cost reduction initiatives and management changes have recently been made as we continue with our plan to make this subsidiary profitable in the future," Itin added.
